text:
ops-bot: PagerDuty alert: elevated 5xx rate for /v1/generate (gateway) — threshold breached 09:12 UTC, paging #incidents

alice-oncall: I'm on it. seeing surge in 5xx/timeouts. metrics look like queue build at the scheduler. assigning to bob and carol.

bob-sre: grabbing traces and logs now. initial look: request latency climbs, scheduler queue length increasing, a small subset of workers stuck on long batches -> head-of-line.

carol-runtime: confirmed from dashboard: batching_queue_depth per-scheduler pod spiked from ~20 -> 400 in 3m. queue_latency p95 -> 1.2s, tail latency huge. many gateway 502/504s reported.

dave-ml: any model-specific changes or recent deploy that could increase per-request time?

alice-oncall: no API deploys in last hour. runtime deploy 6h ago. workload distribution changed — looks like a large burst from a single customer route. chopping up the context?

bob-sre: running promql: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..",route="/v1/generate"}[1m])) by (instance) — shows concentrated 5xx from two pods. Also see long-running tasks at the top of batching queue: 
```
kubectl logs scheduler-7f6 -n inference | tail -n 100
# repeated: processing batch id=xyz duration=8.3s
```

carol-runtime: plan: 1) reduce max_batch_window for schedulers (lower latency) 2) temporarily route traffic off problematic scheduler pods 3) enable fallback_model for heavy routes 4) alert customers if impact large. Thoughts?

dave-ml: fallback_model good. Which variant? use smaller model-quantized v1.2 that has lower latency. Will that create downstream capacity issues? probably ok for short window.

bob-sre: I'll cordon the two overloaded scheduler pods and drain them. command: `kubectl cordon scheduler-7f6 && kubectl drain scheduler-7f6 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — will move work to other pods. Doing a gradual drain to avoid massive reroute.

alice-oncall: assigning mitigation tasks: bob = pod cordon/drain + autoscaler tune, carol = reduce batch window + enable fallback, dave = load test fallback to ensure no quality/regression, eve = customer impact comms + update status page.

eve-support: drafting status update: "We are investigating elevated 5xx+timeout errors on generation endpoints. Engineering is mitigating and we will follow up with root cause." sending to ops channel and support.

bob-sre: cordon initiated on scheduler-7f6. noticed many BATCH_WAIT events. lowering BATCH_MAX_WINDOW on remaining schedulers to 25ms: `kubectl set env deploy/scheduler BATCH_MAX_WINDOW=25ms -n inference` — applying now.

carol-runtime: applying config change to fleet. also toggling `ENABLE_PREFETCH=false` on the heavy route to reduce long-running batches.

dave-ml: firing a smoke against fallback model: `curl -X POST ... -d '{"model":"small-quant-v1.2"}'` - 95th latency ~90ms, looks stable. no immediate reg issues.

bob-sre: draining scheduler-7f6 complete. traffic redistributed. backlog decreased from 400 -> 60 in 8m. 5xx rate fell from 14% -> 4% of traffic.

alice-oncall: good. still seeing intermittent gateway 504s. might be head-of-line from older long-tail KV cache hits. any KV cache hot keys?

carol-runtime: yes, KV-cache miss ratio for some customers jumped. we applied short-term TTL increase for KV to reduce recompute, and disabled KV-aggregation for routes with large context.

bob-sre: autoscaler: increased replica count for scheduler pool by +3 (from 8 -> 11). watch on CPU/GPU utilization.

eve-support: sent update to customers: "We mitigated the surge by reducing batching window and routing to lower-latency model variants. Some requests may still see timeouts while the fleet drains. We're monitoring and will post another update in 30 mins."

dave-ml: running longer load test against full pipeline to ensure we don't regress. initial 30m run looks stable; no OOMs.

alice-oncall: monitoring logs. p95 latency back to baseline, p99 improving. 5xx at ~1.2% now. status page updated.

bob-sre: follow-ups: - collect traces from problematic pod for postmortem - add alert for rapid queue-depth growth (delta over 1m) - consider per-customer rate-limiting for spike protection

carol-runtime: proposed long-term: implement head-of-line avoidance in scheduler (e.g., preempt long-running batches, per-customer queue shards), smarter routing by estimated processing time, autoscaler reactive to queue depth rather than CPU only.

dave-ml: agree. also recommend model admission control for huge context sizes.

alice-oncall: for now incident is mitigated. moving to monitoring state. assigning bob/carol/dave to follow-up postmortem. eve to send final customer update.

eve-support: final sent: "Issue mitigated; services returned to normal. Root cause analysis underway."

ops-bot: Incident log: incident-1772401234 created, severity=high, status=mitigated, responders=[alice-oncall,bob-sre,carol-runtime,dave-ml,eve-support].

alice-oncall: thumbs. will open a postmortem doc and link traces. thanks team. :thumbsup:
